nodes.title: Production trace, model.call rows over 3 days (to 2026-10-15 11:00 UTC): 941. Of these, 933 have sid 'server' (no request context), 6 a real lesson's sid, 2 other; 639 of the 933 took ≤ 2 ms (test stubs). All 95 model.call 429s are sid 'server' and NONE is a real lesson's. The 06 UTC hour held 138 sid='server' taxila-fast chat calls with real latency, and its 49 429s ran 210-516 ms: the main loop's own real-model repro scripts run with .env.local, not children. The 10:48 UTC burst (17 429s, 400 / 500 / 503 / network at 0-1 ms) was this session's 14.3 gate: npm test inherited production's DATABASE_URL, so r5-overflow's stubbed calls were recorded into the production trace. So ms-r142-429-contention's '51 of 361 production taxila-fast calls throttled at 06 UTC while TEST ran' was not child traffic. No child's lesson was throttled in the window measured.

nodes.title: Running the release gate (scripts/deploy-azure.mjs --gate, which loads .env.local) with production's DATABASE_URL in the environment of npm test. What broke: every stubbed model call a test made (fake 429 / 400 / 500 / network at 0-1 ms) was written into the PRODUCTION trace with sid 'server', 639 rows in 3 days. Those rows, and the main loop's own real-model scripts run with .env.local, were then read as production throttling (ms-r142-429-contention). Fix: infra/gate.mjs gateEnv: the gate's commands run in CI's environment, with no DATABASE_URL / DATABASE_URL_DIRECT / TAXILA_DB. The read-only migrations-applied test still reads its URL from .env.local, and the DB suites keep CONDUCTOR_TEST_DATABASE_URL. Rule: anything that runs with .env.local and is not the production server sets DATABASE_URL empty, or points at TEST.

A production number about children (429 rates, latency, failures) counts only trace rows whose sid is a real lesson, i.e. joined to lesson. sid 'server' rows are scripts, tests and background jobs, and are reported separately. The 14.2 overflow lane stands on stream 3's measured arm (+747 ms instead of a failure) and on the structural fact that TEST and production share deployment limits. The claim that production was throttled is withdrawn. TEST traffic still routes to southindia (dc-r143-test-chat-southindia) because the shared limits are real, even though no child was measured throttled.
nodes.reversal: a background-job path that legitimately records child-facing model calls with sid 'server' (then it needs its own lesson attribution)

md.measurements:
## ms-r143-prod-trace-origin (2026-10-15), correcting ms-r142-429-contention

- Production model.call rows over 3 days: 941. 933 have sid 'server', 6 are real lessons, 2 other.
- Of the 933 server rows, 639 took ≤ 2 ms (test stubs).
- All 95 429s are sid 'server'; none belongs to a child's lesson.
- The 06 UTC 429s were the main loop's own repro scripts. The 10:48 burst was the 14.3 gate's tests, written to production.
- **"Production was throttled" is withdrawn.**
md.rejected:
## rj-r143-gate-wrote-prod-trace (2026-10-15)

- **Tried:** the release gate ran npm test with production's DATABASE_URL in its environment.
- **What broke:** stubbed model calls were written into the production trace (639 rows in 3 days) and misread as production throttling.
- **Fix:** gateEnv runs the gate in CI's environment, with no database URL.
md.decisions:
## dc-r143-prod-numbers-need-a-lesson-sid (2026-10-15)

- **What:** a production number about children counts only rows whose sid is a real lesson. sid 'server' rows are scripts, tests and background jobs.
- **Why:** see ms-r143-prod-trace-origin. The overflow lane and the TEST routing stand on the arm and on the shared limits, not on a throttled child.
- **Reversal:** a background path that legitimately records child-facing calls with sid 'server'.
